mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 24,000 billion dollars indicates robust economic growth, which typically supports corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters where GDPC1 exceeds 24,000 billion dollars, or the Rank IC over 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months signals aggressive monetary tightening, which typically increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500 thousand units signal strong consumer demand and economic momentum, which typically supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, HOUST growth does not correlate with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or returns are negative in more than 55% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 330 (indicating elevated inflation) typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market anticipates tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 330, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tight labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE falls below 4.0%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand across multiple sectors, which typically supports economic growth and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.0 signals economic weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In supply-constrained regimes, INDPRO decline does not correlate with negative 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or returns are positive in more than 55% of such instances.
